profile.headline: Software Engineer at Tapestry Solutions
profile.summary:
I am a computer scientist and cyber security professional.  My research involves me interviewing federal and local law enforcement, prosecutors and defense attorneys, as well as a number of individuals involved in some high profile internet scams.  I occasionally consult on data breaches and perform pen testing, usually for small businesses that can't afford to pay a big firm for incident response.

I talk to black hats/grey hats all the time.  As a result, I've developed a healthy paranoia of some (but not all of) them.  They deserve respect and acknowledgement for their skill set, but need to be constantly reminded of the ethics and laws of digital privacy.  The best way to do that is to understand them and their motives.  While getting inside the mind of other hackers can prove to be difficult (and, definitely, not the best advice I can give), it is the best way I know to understand them.  Hopefully, with this understanding, you can protect yourself by being aware of the issues/threats looming online and in our own homes.  

I am a proponent of the Defense in Depth model because there are too many ways to be targeted and no one strategy works for everything.  No matter how good you are, you're gonna get violated if you surf the web.  So, you better have a backup plan when prevention fails. 

I perform research in malware and investigate all sides of the issue.  Hopefully, I can contribute to the education and understanding of people regarding online privacy and security.

projects.title: Identifying Arson in a Blighted Urban Area
projects.description: A small Illinois town with a dwindling population has been plagued with an unusually high number of fire incidents over the last 10 years.  Although it has one of the smallest populations in the region, it makes up more than 80% of the fire incidents in the county.  Using data analytics, and adjusted grid mappings, a visualization of the incident locations and the nearest fire engine house will be built to discern a pattern for determining how many of the fires, if any, are being intentionally set and whether the State Fire Marshal needs to get involved.

projects.title: Academic Requirements for Designation as a Center of Academic Excellence in Cyber Operations
projects.description:
Assisting cyber security program coordinator in providing necessary documentation of projects, materials, interdepartmental collaborations, community outreach and academic studies for Washington University in St Louis Cyber Security Master's program application to be certified and accredited by the National Security Agency as a Center of Academic Excellence (CAE).

During this process, I developed a class on practical malware analysis for several semesters which was popular enough to be re-branded and integrated into several programs including Defensive Hacking, Information Visualization, Predictive Modeling, Systems Programming and Telecommunications. 

The accreditation committee has encouraged the changes and continues to provide feedback to us.
